meaning: Small files a website saves in your browser to remember you, such as your login or cart. Some track you across sites.
clues: Your browser saves small bits of data about the sites you visit.
Saved details help a page remember your visit or choices.
They can keep you signed in or remember what is in a shopping cart.
Some track what you do on more than one website.
The word is also a baked treat.
assumes: Browsing history is a list of pages you visited
A browser cache keeps copies of files so pages can load faster
Autofill stores information you enter into forms

decoys.meaning: A list of websites and pages you visited.
Saved copies of website files that help pages load faster next time.
A browser feature that fills common form details, such as your name or address.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: You can clear site files in your browser settings. Read the choice first, because it may sign you out.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: A record can be useful, but you should know where it is kept. We kept receipts in a drawer.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Some sites need these files for a cart or sign-in. Others use them to track activity.

sources.name: FTC, How Websites and Apps Collect and Use Your Information
